errata.defect: The child reached through namelist (state s01) tests its Var1 with conf:idVal, which the XPath template specializes to `$Var1/text() =1`. A namelist entry passes the value of the parent location `$Var1`, which in the XPath data model is the parent's datamodel <data id="Var1"> element (SCXML 1.0 CR 2014-03-13 C.3.1: the processor MUST bind an XPath variable to that <data> element), and the child inserts that value as the child of its own <data> element. The value 1 is therefore at `$Var1/data/text()`, which is exactly what official case 240 checks for the identical namelist-to-child situation with conf:namelistIdVal. With conf:idVal the namelist child always reports failure while the param child (s03) reports success, so the case cannot pass for any conforming XPath processor.
evidence: upstream/sources/240/test240.txml:27 `<transition conf:namelistIdVal="1=1" target="subFinal1">` (same namelist semantics, correct attribute)
templates/xpath.xsl:448-453 conf:namelistIdVal: `test that given var whose value was passed in via namelist has specific value` -> `$Var1/data/text()`
errata.correction: Use conf:namelistIdVal (as official case 240 does) for the namelist-fed child only; the param-fed children keep conf:idVal.

errata.defect: The only child of case 244 receives Var1 through namelist but tests it with conf:idVal (`$Var1/text() =1`). Under the XPath data model the namelist value is the parent's <data id="Var1"> element, inserted as the child of the child's <data> element (SCXML 1.0 CR 2014-03-13 C.3.1), so the value is at `$Var1/data/text()`, which official case 240 checks with conf:namelistIdVal. As written the case reports failure for every conforming XPath processor.
evidence: upstream/sources/240/test240.txml:27 `<transition conf:namelistIdVal="1=1" target="subFinal1">` (same namelist semantics, correct attribute)
errata.correction: Use conf:namelistIdVal, as official case 240 does for the same namelist-fed child.

errata.defect: The XPath template specializes conf:varNonexistentStruct with ECMAScript member syntax, `$Var1.bar`, which XPath 1.0 parses as a reference to an undeclared variable named `Var1.bar` rather than a non-existent substructure of the loaded Var1. Manual case 307 compares accessing a late-bound variable before load with accessing a non-existent substructure of a loaded variable; with an undeclared-variable reference in the second log the two outputs the W3C instruction asks the tester to compare measure different things.
evidence: templates/xpath.xsl:112-115 `<!-- an expr that is the value of a non-existent substructure of a variable -->` ... `$Var<xsl:value-of select="." />.bar`
templates/ecmascript.xsl:114-116 the ECMAScript template emits `Var1.bar`, the member access this syntax denotes in ECMAScript
upstream/sources/307/test307.txml:28 `<log label="entering s1, value of non-existent substructure of Var 1 is: " conf:varNonexistentStruct="1"/>`
errata.correction: Emit the XPath form of a non-existent substructure, `$Var1/bar` (a child step of the variable's <data> element, SCXML 1.0 CR 2014-03-13 C.3.1). Not corrected: the label-only logs `no error in s0`/`No error in s1` are authored upstream as conf:expr="" (upstream/sources/307/test307.txml:18 and :36) and both official templates copy that verbatim into `<log expr="">`; that is the test's own convention for a log without a value, so the erratum leaves it unchanged.

errata.defect: conf:messageBodyEquals is specialized without quoting its value, producing `contains($_event/raw, this+is+some+content)` (an XPath arithmetic expression over child steps, not the string literal) and `contains($_event/raw, this%20is%20some%20content)` (an XPath syntax error). Neither guard can test that the received body contains the sent content.
errata.correction: Quote the value as an XPath string literal, as every other _event/raw template in xpath.xsl does (lines 360 and 366).

errata.defect: conf:eventNamedParamHasValue matches its value with the regex `([0-9]+)(\s+)(\S+)`, so only numeric parameter names are recognized. The value `_scxmleventname test` has no match and the template emits `cond=""`, an empty guard, so the case cannot test that the event name was sent as the _scxmleventname parameter.
evidence: templates/ecmascript.xsl:698-700 the ECMAScript template matches the same attribute with `(\S+)(\s+)(\S+)`
errata.correction: Match any non-blank parameter name, `(\S+)(\s+)(\S+)`, as the official ECMAScript template does, yielding `contains($_event/raw, '_scxmleventname=test')`.
